extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for the NIGMS NRSA Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship (F32)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an NIGMS Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA Individual Postdoctoral (F32) fellowship application, including eligibility, institutional expectations, length of support, and factors used in funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant doctoral degree requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have received the doctoral degree (Ph.D., M.D., D.O., D.C., D.D.S., D.V.M., O.D., D.P.M., Sc.D., Eng.D., Dr.P.H., D.N.S., N.D., Pharm.D., D.S.W., Psy.D. or equivalent doctoral degree from an accredited domestic or foreign institution) by the beginning date of the proposed award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree may be from domestic or foreign accredited institution; equivalency to listed degrees is recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree-specific training expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants holding the Ph.D. degree, this award is designed to provide support for advanced and specialized training in basic research, in basic research associated with clinical problems or in clinical research. For applicants holding the M.D. or other clinical-professional degree, this program is intended to provide at least 2 years of rigorous basic or clinical research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should tailor proposed training to these expectations depending on the applicant's degree (i.e., Ph.D. applicants: advanced/specialized basic research training; clinical-professional degree holders: at least two years of rigorous basic or clinical research training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional setting and sponsor acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant's proposed study must include the conduct of research with supervision or other opportunity for guidance appropriate to his or her background and objectives. Prior to submitting an application, an applicant must arrange for acceptance at an appropriate training institution by a responsible sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institutional setting may be domestic or foreign, private or public. The application must document the availability of staff and facilities required for the proposed research and for accomplishing the applicant's training objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate length of NRSA postdoctoral support
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policy is to provide up to 3 years of aggregate Kirschstein-NRSA support at the postdoctoral level, including any combination of support from institutional training grants (e.g. T32) and an individual fellowship award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When calculating requested support length, include prior NRSA support at the postdoctoral level; total aggregate across mechanisms should not exceed 3 years absent special considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of extenuating circumstances for interruptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extenuating circumstance leading to interruptions in research training may be considered for competitive applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential applicants should consult program staff to discuss individual situations before submitting an application; documentation/supporting explanation may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of new training experiences / broadening skills
rubrics_metrics.description: The F32 program is designed to support research training experiences in new settings to maximize the acquisition of new skills and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing postdoctoral training at the applicant's doctoral institution, the application must carefully document the opportunities for new research training experiences specifically designed to broaden the candidate's scientific background and describe new knowledge and/or technical skills to be acquired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding consideration: priority score
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by NIGMS as one of the factors staff consider when making funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding consideration: training potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIGMS staff consider the applicant's potential to benefit from and succeed in the proposed training as a factor in funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding consideration: details of the training program
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clarity, rigor, and appropriateness of the proposed training program are explicitly considered by NIGMS staff in funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding consideration: time already spent in sponsor's laboratory
rubrics_metrics.description: Time already spent in the sponsor's laboratory
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIGMS staff assess how much prior time the applicant has spent in the sponsor's lab when evaluating the application (e.g., to gauge novelty of the training experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding consideration: program relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relevance of the proposed research/training to NIGMS's scientific programs is a factor in funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding consideration: summary statement narrative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of the summary statement narrative (peer review critiques) is considered by NIGMS staff when making funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research area eligibility (NIGMS interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral fellowships support research in all areas of interest to NIGMS (organized into Fellowship Support Areas), including those described in these specific areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure proposed research fits within NIGMS's stated areas of interest and consult the listed Fellowship Support Areas for alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and stipend information
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information regarding dates of application and notification, tenure, eligibility, payback requirements and stipends may be found at the NIH Research Training website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative details (including stipend levels, application dates, payback obligations, and tenure specifics) are maintained on the NIH Research Training site and should be consulted when preparing the application.
